title: Classify failures by lifecycle stage
summary: A managed Colab job should report which stage failed: ALLOCATION, SECRET_STAGE, INPUT_UPLOAD, INSTALL, WORKER_RESOURCE_GATE, EXECUTE/WORKLOAD, OUTPUT_DOWNLOAD, GRADING/PROMOTION, STOP, or SECRET_RETIRE. Do not collapse a missing final output into 'the model failed' when execution never began. During Gemma recovery, distinct incidents included unsupported CLI flags before allocation, connection loss during install, GPU-memory rejection before model load, a Transformers API failure before training step 1, a Debian extraction failure after completed training, upload failure before regrade model load, and finally genuine generated-code quality rejection after all infrastructure passed.
evidence_note: Grounded in the full live Gemma-ooRexx Colab recovery/regrade sequence. This taxonomy exists specifically to prevent infrastructure faults from being mistaken for workload/model faults and vice versa.
invariants: Record the deepest completed stage and the failing stage.
Promotion/grading is separate from training/execution success.
OUTPUT_MISSING is a symptom; preserve the earlier stage evidence that explains why output is absent.
A rejected quality gate may still contain a valuable trained artifact; do not discard it automatically.
